caption: Layer grouping patterns, where the horizontal and vertical axes represent groups (G_1, , G_4) and numbers of layers in groups.
model_annotation: The figure illustrates five schematic layer grouping patterns (“Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck”), each shown as a small vertical bar chart intended to represent the number of layers assigned to four groups (G₁ to G₄). In each mini-chart, the categorical axis is horizontal with four implied group positions (left to right corresponding to G₁, G₂, G₃, G₄ as stated in the caption), but individual group tick labels are not drawn; the value axis is vertical and represents “numbers of layers in groups,” though no axis title, numeric tick marks, units, or explicit scale are shown. All bars are filled with a pale/light green color and have thin dark outlines. In the “Increasing” pattern, the four bars rise stepwise from left to right, with the first bar shortest and the fourth bar tallest (a monotonic increase in bar height). In the “Uniform” pattern, all four bars are drawn at the same height, forming a flat profile across the four group positions. In the “Decreasing” pattern, the four bars descend from left to right, with the first bar tallest and the fourth bar shortest (a monotonic decrease in bar height). In the “Spindle” pattern, the first and fourth bars are short while the middle two bars (second and third) are taller and drawn at approximately the same height, creating a symmetric “low–high–high–low” profile. In the “Bottleneck” pattern, the first and fourth bars are tall while the two middle bars are shorter and approximately equal, giving a “high–low–low–high” profile. The bars within each mini-chart appear ordered by group index (G₁→G₄) rather than sorted by value, and there are no annotations, legends, or visual emphasis beyond the consistent coloring and outlines.
